sermon.title: A Powerful Side of Eternal Life Part 2 How Important Can Eternal Life be to Us Individually?
sermon.series: A Powerful Side of Eternal Life
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues his teaching that eternal life is a personal, intimate, resulting encounter with God and Jesus Christ, using the new covenant promise that all shall know the Lord, Paul’s desire to know Christ, and Job’s “I know that my Redeemer lives.” He shares how his own encounter kept him consistent, then argues that the Bible calls people to repentance rather than therapy. He closes by saying a big crowd is not God’s approval and asking listeners whether they have ever really met the Master.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: he says “John 5:20,” but the words he reads (“we know that the Son of God has come and has given us an understanding”) are 1 John 5:20; he says about 4,000 were added to the church when Peter preached, whereas Acts 2:41 says about three thousand; the caption text for the ministry he calls “Melodyland” was garbled in several places and has been written as that one name; one first name after the Exodus International comment (about 18:44) was not clear and is marked [unclear].

chunks.section_question: Who can know the Lord under the new covenant? (Hebrews 8:11)
chunks.short_answer: He says the new covenant promises that all shall know the Lord, “from the least of them to the greatest,” and that this personal knowing is “not just the Pentecostals, not just the Baptist, everyone that believes and comes can have” it. He says it is “not limited, it’s in the covenant.”
chunks.text: Hallelujah. Now, Hebrews 8:11, this is the new covenant: “None shall teach his neighbor and his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ for all shall know Me, from the least of them to the greatest.” All shall have a personal, intimate, resulting encounter with Jesus Christ. That’s in the covenant. Not just the Pentecostals, not just the Baptist, everyone that believes and comes can have this personal knowing of Jesus Christ. Amen. Not limited, it’s in the covenant. And if you feel wimpy, they got the word “least” in there. If you feel like you’re a mighty man of God already, they got the “greatest” in there. You still need it. Amen.

chunks.section_question: Do we still know Christ only as He was in the flesh? (2 Corinthians 5:16)
chunks.short_answer: He says we have heard the story of Jesus’ life, death and resurrection, but Paul says we know Him that way no longer because He is risen, on His throne, and with us in Spirit as “Christ in us, the hope of glory.” He says this is “the difference between being born again and just a believer.”
chunks.text: 2 Corinthians 5:16: “Though we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet we know Him thus no longer.” Okay. We heard the story: Jesus came and He was born of a virgin, and He, you know, lived with His parents, and, you know, He went to the temple and dazzled the scribes and the priests there in the temple with His knowledge of the Scriptures, and then He went back and He became a carpenter, and then, you know, He got baptized, and got baptized in the Holy Ghost, and preached and did miracles and all that, and died on the cross and rose. We know that part of Jesus. Amen. But what Paul said, “For this reason, I’m sorry, yet now we know Him that way no longer.” Why? Because He’s not in the flesh anymore. He has risen. He is in His throne in heaven. He poured out Himself back in the church on the day of Pentecost. He is with us now in Spirit. We don’t know Him just in the flesh. We know Him what? As Christ in us, the hope of glory, the Spirit of Christ. Can I hear an amen? And we know Him. “For this reason, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creature; old things have passed away, and all things become new.” See, this is the difference between being born again and just a believer. And the Congregationalists were right: the Bible plainly tells us there is power in the birthing in our new spiritual life. And eternal life is that encounter with Jesus Christ. Isn’t that powerful? Hallelujah.

chunks.section_question: What does Paul mean by “that I may know Him”? (Philippians 3:10)
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul counted everything he gained in this world as worthless compared to knowing Christ and the power of His resurrection. He says too many people stay at the blood and the death, but “we have a resurrected Savior,” and that Christianity is “not a philosophy, it’s a reality.”
chunks.text: Philippians 3:10 says, “That I may know Jesus.” I count all things worthless, anything I gain in this world, Paul says I count it as dung. I wanted the knowledge of Christ, and I want to know Him and the power of His resurrection. You see, too many people stay at the blood and the death, but we have a resurrected Savior, and the same Spirit that raised Christ from the dead dwells where? In us. Folks, that’s what makes Christianity different. We have a living God that lives in us, guides us, directs us, empowers us. This is not a philosophy, it’s a reality. You can’t reduce Christianity down just to another philosophy. An encounter with a supernatural God is a very powerful thing.

chunks.section_question: What is the understanding Jesus has given us? (1 John 5:20)
chunks.short_answer: He reads that Jesus has given us an understanding, and says that understanding is not only being saved by grace through faith but “that we may know Him,” a “personal, intimate, resulting encounter that changes my life.” He says those who deny that Jesus is the true and only God are “antichrist; they’re opposing who Christ is.”
chunks.text: John 5:20: “We know the Son of God has come and given us an understanding.” Now listen to this. This we know, that Jesus Christ has come, and this Jesus has given us an understanding. Now what is that understanding? That I’m saved by grace through faith? No. That we may know Him: personal, intimate, resulting encounter that changes my life. I’m a new creature. “We know Him who is true. He’s given us an understanding that we are in Him,” Jesus Christ. And look at this: “This is the true God and eternal life.” Now, I submit to you two questions. Is Jesus the true and only God according to this verse? People that say He is not are antichrist; they’re opposing who Christ is.

chunks.section_question: How did knowing God change his life, and do you have to be a preacher to know Him?
chunks.short_answer: He tells of repenting at the altar and feeling “the weight of sin just lift off,” then being filled with the baptism of the Holy Spirit and having the Word revealed “line upon line, precept upon precept.” He says others who got saved with him backslid but he stayed consistent “because I experienced these things,” and that you don’t have to be a preacher for God to come to you personally.
chunks.text:
Now, I submit to you another thing. Did Jesus give us the mental understanding that we could know Him? Absolutely. Is it in His new covenant? Absolutely. And then He explains what knowing is. And I don’t know about you, but this is what changed my life. See, when I actually went up to the altar and repented of my sins, I had an encounter with God there. Literally, I felt the weight of sin just lift off my life. I didn’t even know I had it. When I got filled with the baptism of the Holy Spirit, the love and the power that came, and the force within me to go to the Word and learn the Word. You see, I experienced these things. I experienced salvation, I experienced the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and I experienced the Word being revealed to me little by little, line upon line, precept upon precept, and it made the difference in the world in my life. And while others that got saved when I got saved, and in the area I got saved, departed and went their own way and backslid, I stayed consistent. Why? Because I experienced these things in my life.

And when troubles come, they didn’t trouble me. When temptation come, I didn’t have to give in to it. Are you there? I’m just trying to give you an illustration. Mr. Barnes, he’s been around ever since I’ve known him. Say it’s not just me, I know all kinds of people. They’re not famous, they don’t write books, but Christ was real to them. They know Him, and they stayed consistent with Him. Hallelujah. I mean, you know, you don’t have to be a preacher to know God and be a light to the world. That’s right. You don’t have to be a preacher for God to come to you and personally cause you to experience the things of God. Absolutely. They’re for all of us.

chunks.section_question: What did Job know about his Redeemer? (Job 19:25)
chunks.short_answer: He says Job used the word “I know” and had “a personal, intimate, resulting encounter with my God,” even without Scripture telling him Jesus would come back to the earth. He says Job knew that after his body was gone “in my flesh I will see Him,” and “that’s eternal life.”
chunks.text: Now, in Job, this isn’t a new thing. In Job, I love this verse. I can still remember reading my Bible through for the first time, and this verse just woke me up. This message has been around. See, Job is back there when Abraham lived, long time ago. I know. Job 19:25: “That my Redeemer lives.” See, he used that word “I know.” I’ve had a personal, intimate, resulting encounter with my God. He said, “He shall stand at last on the earth.” Job had no Scripture telling him that Jesus Christ was going to come back to the earth after He came the first time. “He is, Jesus shall stand at the last day on the earth after my skin is destroyed.” After I die, “this I know, that in my flesh I will see God, whom I will see for myself.” He said, yes, my body is going to go to the grave, the worms are going to eat me, but I know my Redeemer is going to come in the last day, and in my flesh I will see Him. That’s eternal life. That’s exactly what Paul said, wasn’t it? And folks, with this kind of an encounter and experience, let me tell you, Christianity is just a motor. I mean, it’s a powerful engine within you driving you upward all the time. Amen.

chunks.section_question: Why does knowing Jesus decide where you spend eternity? (Luke 23:43)
chunks.short_answer: He says that if eternal life is knowing Him, the end result is spending eternity with Jesus, while those who reject Him “will spend eternity away from Jesus, because we’re all born into eternity.” He points to Jesus telling the thief on the cross, “Today you’re going to be with Me in paradise.”
chunks.text: Hallelujah. Luke 23:43: “Today shall you be with Me in paradise.” Okay, He turned to the thief on the cross, one of them, and said, “Today you’re going to be with Me in paradise.” Why is that important? Because if eternal life is knowing Him, then what is, you know, what’s the end result? The end result is I spend eternity with Jesus, while you that reject Him and don’t want to know Him will spend eternity away from Jesus, because we’re all born into eternity. But this is eternal life, that I may know Him, that I may spend eternity with Jesus Christ. Hallelujah. “To be absent in the body is to be present with the Lord.” That is eternal life. Did you get it?

chunks.section_question: If the Bible only mentions a sin a few times, is it a small issue?
chunks.short_answer: He recounts answering the argument that the Bible opposes homosexuality only six times by asking how many times it opposes stealing, and how many times it mentions sex with children. His point: “If the Bible mentions it one time, it’s law.”
chunks.text: Now let me talk about my opponents for a little bit. Okay, talking to homosexuals recently, their argument was that the Bible only opposes homosexuality six times, so therefore it’s not a big issue. I said, “Sir, how many times does the Bible oppose stealing?” Well, they don’t know, of course, and neither do you, because I’m in debates with them and I got to get answers. I’m fighting with them, I’m trying to free them. I said, “Eight times. Does that mean stealing is okay?” I said, “Let me ask you again, sir. How many times in the Bible is sex with children mentioned?” And they go, “Well, it says, you know, you’ve got to not offend the little kids, and not, but it doesn’t say, ‘Thou shalt not have sex with children.’” I said, “How many times does the Bible say that?” And of course they don’t know. I said, “Zero.” I said, “Are you telling me it’s okay to have sex with an 8-year-old kid, a four-year-old kid?” I said, “Your argument is stupid. If the Bible mentions it one time, it’s law.” Amen.

chunks.section_question: Can therapy change people, or does it take the power of knowing Christ?
chunks.short_answer: He says he watched churches “go from the power of the Word to therapy,” both telling people it is okay and not okay to be homosexual, and says “therapy is not in the Bible.” He says one therapy group’s leaders left it, and concludes “therapy doesn’t work. The power of knowing Christ does.”
chunks.text:
Exodus International is a group that started in Melodyland Church back in the ‘60s, ‘70s. They used reparative therapy, they called it, “pray the gay away,” to get homosexuals to stop being homosexual. Therapy is a mental, medical way of trying to get people to change behavior or physical deficiencies and so forth. All right. And I watched this psycho stuff coming into the church. All right, I watched churches go from the power of the Word to therapy. And Melodyland was the leader of it, one of the leaders. Big church, famous people come from all over to go there to their charismatic conferences and so forth. And I’ve been to a couple of them myself, not the conferences but meetings where special, like David Wilkerson came in. They were very powerful, but you can’t stay powerful if you build on the wrong foundation. So through therapy, even today, they’re trying to treat human behavior through mental treatment, trying to convince them, talk them out of it. And the other side’s the same thing. I saw a documentary, and other Christians are trying to tell homosexuals, this group, they brought these young people in and said, “Now look in the mirror.” They looked in the mirror. “Now who do you see?” “That’s me.” I said, “Now say, ‘I see a child of God.’” And they would say, “I see a child of God.” See, “Now you’re a child of God.” So we got therapy going on on both sides: it’s okay to be a homosexual, it’s not okay being a homosexual. Let me tell you, folks, therapy is not in the Bible. Are you there?

And it wasn’t in there when I was a young Christian, and I stood up to Melodyland back there as a young Christian. I challenged them because they challenged me. They said I was teaching a bad doctrine, so we got into a little corral once, and I won that corral. The people lied. I wasn’t teaching that at all. They said I was teaching Jesus wasn’t coming. I didn’t teach that. I just didn’t teach He was coming the way they were teaching, that’s all. Hallelujah. Now, Melodyland was a round church. It used to be the Melodyland Theater, and big singers and everything come there, and then they turned it into this charismatic center. And of course it failed. And the leaders of this Exodus International, two leaders, Gary Cooper, who died from AIDS, left the group. These were the ones that were changing homosexuals’ lives. They left the group with a man named Michael [unclear]. They both left their wives and they lived in a homosexual relationship, and Gary died of AIDS. And what’s the point here? Therapy doesn’t work. The power of knowing Christ does. If we don’t have power of the Word, power of the Spirit, power of Jesus, we have nothing more than the world does.

It used to be the Melodyland Theater, and big singers and everything come there, and then they turned it into this charismatic center. And of course it failed. And the leaders of this Exodus International, two leaders, Gary Cooper, who died from AIDS, left the group. These were the ones that were changing homosexuals’ lives. They left the group with a man named Michael [unclear]. They both left their wives and they lived in a homosexual relationship, and Gary died of AIDS. And what’s the point here? Therapy doesn’t work. The power of knowing Christ does. If we don’t have power of the Word, power of the Spirit, power of Jesus, we have nothing more than the world does.

chunks.section_question: What does the Bible use to change people: therapy or repentance?
chunks.short_answer: He says “the Bible never uses therapy to change people’s lives. The Bible uses repentance”: admit you are wrong, confess you have violated God’s Word, turn from the way you were going, and go to Christ and the Word. He says this “is the power of the gospel under salvation” and can’t be replaced with therapy or psychology.
chunks.text: Now, the Bible never uses therapy to change people’s lives. The Bible uses repentance. The Bible says repent. The Bible says admit you’re wrong, confess that you’re wrong, that you have violated God’s Word. The Bible says use self-control. We’ve got to preach repentance. Repent means you turn from what you were doing, the way you were going. It’s your responsibility to turn and denounce that wrong and admit you were wrong and go to Christ and go to that Word, and He will build you up, because He can’t lie. You can’t replace that with therapy, you can’t replace that with psychology. That is the power of the gospel under salvation.

chunks.section_question: Can someone believe in God and still not be free from sin?
chunks.short_answer: He says he knows people who believe in God and think they are Christians “but they’re not free. Why? Because they don’t know Him.” He says that until a person decides to repent and follow the Word, “the thief is going to stay a thief, the drug addict is going to stay a drug addict,” and that people want to keep what they’re doing and still go to heaven.
chunks.text: Amen. And we saw back there that believers were not free. And there’s a lot of homosexuals I know that believe in God and they believe they’re Christians, but they’re not free. Why? Because they don’t know Him. I can pray in tongues, I can pray in English, I can pray with fortitude, I can pray with theatrics, but until they decide to repent and admit they’re wrong and follow the Word and seek the Word and seek Jesus, they are going to stay a homosexual. The thief is going to stay a thief. The drug addict is going to stay a drug addict. Now, is that the gospel? Yeah. Nowhere in the Bible do you find them using therapy. They used the Word of God and it worked. Of course, people can reject it, but see, they want to reject it but they want acceptance in the rejection. They still want to go to heaven, but they want to reject repentance, they want to reject self-control, they want to keep doing what they’re doing, but they still want to go to heaven. So they want you to approve their belief as a justifiable way to get into heaven.

chunks.section_question: Should churches rely on programs and spectacle to draw a crowd?
chunks.short_answer: He says some circles get “hooped up in the Spirit” without preaching repentance, and others get hooped up in programs and theatrics, with the next attraction always bigger. He says “that ain’t what the Bible people did. They preached the word and the Lord added to the church as He saw fit.”
chunks.text: Now that was a good statement. And so in the Pentecostal circles, we get all hooped up in the Spirit and the presence and, you know, tongues and prophecy and all this, and we’re not preaching repentance and people aren’t getting delivered. And outside those circles they’re all hooped up in programs and, you know, theatrics of special programs and, you know, bring an elephant in and get the people to come in, and what are you going to do next Sunday? You got to bring a tiger in to get the people to come in. And what do you do next? Well, you got to have a skydiver come down and land in the parking lot. You know, that ain’t what the Bible people did. They preached the word and the Lord added to the church as He saw fit.

chunks.section_question: Is a big crowd a sign of God’s approval?
chunks.short_answer: He says “the crowd is not God’s approval,” because the crowd left Jesus when He asked for commitment and He kept the same message, being after disciples and a personal encounter. He closes by asking whether you have ever really met the Master and had an encounter where the power touched your life.
chunks.text:
Melodyland was one of the first mega churches. It doesn’t even exist today, and I knew it wouldn’t exist. Crystal Cathedral doesn’t exist today, and I told the church when it was built it wouldn’t exist, because they’re not building on the right foundations. Yeah, it looks good because they got numbers, but in the end God’s going to bring it down. I can remember telling the church, the crowd is not God’s approval. Look in your Bible: the crowd left Him when He asked for commitment. They left Him. Did Jesus change His message? No. Jesus was after disciples. He was after people that He could know, have an intimate, personal encounter with, turn them into a new creature, change their life. That’s what Jesus was interested in, whether it was 12, 70, or 5,000. And if the crowd left, He kept the same message. When Paul, all of Asia rejected Paul, did Paul change his message? No, he didn’t. And yet people will flock to Saddleback Church because they got 30-some thousand. They’re about the sixth largest church in America, something like that. They’ll flock there because the crowd, they think in their mind, means success, and he’s preaching a very distorted gospel. See, we’re known by fruits. The lead church is known by its leadership, and the church. Are you with me?

Hallelujah. I submit to you today that this is eternal life: a personal, intimate, resulting encounter with God. That third leg of the three-legged stool. Have you ever really met the Master? Have you ever really had an encounter with God where you knew the power had come into you, had touched your life?

faqs.question: What does he say is the result of a personal encounter with the Holy Spirit?
faqs.answer: He says the result is power to be a witness, evidence and proof, in Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria and the uttermost parts of the world. He says it was not power to roll on the floor or “dance like a chicken.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: But you shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you shall be witnesses to Me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.”

faqs.question: How does he define eternal life?
faqs.answer: He says “eternal life is a personal, intimate, resulting encounter, resulting meeting with God and Jesus Christ.” He calls it the third leg of the three-legged stool from his earlier message.

faqs.question: Is this personal knowing of God only for Pentecostals or Baptists?
faqs.answer: No. He says it is “in the covenant, not just the Pentecostals, not just the Baptist, everyone that believes and comes can have this personal knowing of Jesus Christ.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: None of them shall teach his neighbor, and none his brother, saying, ‘Know the LORD,’ for all shall know Me, from the least of them to the greatest of them.

faqs.question: What does he say is the difference between being born again and just a believer?
faqs.answer: He says we no longer know Christ only “in the flesh”; we know Him “as Christ in us, the hope of glory,” and “if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creature.” He says “this is the difference between being born again and just a believer.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.

faqs.question: Does he say Jesus is the true and only God?
faqs.answer: He reads the verse and says “this is the true God and eternal life,” asking whether Jesus is the true and only God according to it. He says people who say He is not are “antichrist; they’re opposing who Christ is.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And we know that the Son of God has come and has given us an understanding, that we may know Him who is true; and we are in Him who is true, in His Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God and eternal life.

faqs.question: What does he say happened when he repented and was baptized in the Holy Spirit?
faqs.answer: He says he “felt the weight of sin just lift off,” then was filled with the baptism of the Holy Spirit, with love, power and a drive to learn the Word. He says he experienced salvation, the baptism of the Holy Ghost and the Word being revealed little by little.

faqs.question: Do you have to be a preacher to know God?
faqs.answer: No. He says there are all kinds of people who are not famous and don’t write books but Christ was real to them, and “you don’t have to be a preacher to know God and be a light to the world.”

faqs.question: What did Job say about seeing God?
faqs.answer: He says Job knew his Redeemer lives and would stand on the earth, and that “in my flesh I will see God, whom I will see for myself.” He adds, “That’s eternal life.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For I know that my Redeemer lives, And He shall stand at last on the earth;

faqs.question: Who does he say will spend eternity away from Jesus?
faqs.answer: He says those who reject Jesus and don’t want to know Him “will spend eternity away from Jesus,” and that everyone is born into eternity; the question is what place you spend it. He says eternal life is knowing Him and spending eternity with Him.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And Jesus said to him, “Assuredly, I say to you, today you will be with Me in Paradise.”

faqs.question: How many times must the Bible mention something for it to be law?
faqs.answer: He says that “if the Bible mentions it one time, it’s law,” and illustrates it by asking how many times the Bible mentions stealing, and how many times it says not to have sex with children.

faqs.question: Is therapy found in the Bible?
faqs.answer: He says “therapy is not in the Bible” and that it wasn’t there when he was a young Christian. He says he watched churches move from the power of the Word to therapy, which he describes as a mental, medical way of trying to change behavior.

faqs.question: What does “repent” mean according to this message?
faqs.answer: He says “repent means you turn from what you were doing, the way you were going.” It is your responsibility to turn, denounce the wrong, admit you were wrong, and go to Christ and the Word, and “He will build you up because He can’t lie.”

faqs.question: Can a person pray in tongues and still need to repent?
faqs.answer: He says he can pray in tongues, in English, with fortitude or with theatrics, “but until they decide to repent and admit they’re wrong and follow the Word and seek the Word and seek Jesus,” they stay as they are.

faqs.question: Is the crowd a sign of God’s approval?
faqs.answer: No. He says, “the crowd is not God’s approval,” noting the crowd left Jesus when He asked for commitment, and that Paul did not change his message when the province of Asia rejected him.

faqs.question: What question does he leave listeners with?
faqs.answer: He asks, “Have you ever really met the Master? Have you ever really had an encounter with God where you knew the power had come into you, had touched your life?”
